292476435_57748566.text: To define the neuronal populations underlying selective thalamic vulnerability, we subclustered thalamic neurons and identified four major neuronal populations composed of two excitatory and two inhibitory neuronal subtypes (Figure 2A-C). Cell-type annotation was guided by previously reported human thalamic transcriptional signatures (Bakken et al., 2021;Marsan et al., 2023;Mathys et al., 2024;Siletti et al., 2023), and refined using the large scale and cross-cohort structure of our integrated dataset. These neuronal populations were distinguished by robust transcriptional signatures, including pan-inhibitory expression of GAD2 and MEIS2 together with differential expression of SOX14, NR2F2, ERBB4, LAMP5, and BCL11B across inhibitory neuronal populations. While InNeu SOX14+ neurons correspond to midbrain-derived interneurons, the InNeu SOX14population is composed of ganglionic eminence-derived subtypes, encompassing medial ganglionic eminence (MGE; marked by LHX6, SST, and NPY) and caudal ganglionic eminence (CGE; marked by CXCL14, VIP, and LAMP5) lineages (Supplementary Figure 2A). In contrast, excitatory neuronal populations were defined by SLC17A6 expression, consistent with thalamic projection neuron identity, and differential RNF220 expression (Figure 2A,B). We therefore annotated these populations as InNeu SOX14+, InNeu SOX14-, ExNeu RNF220+, and ExNeu RNF220-(Figure 2C). Integration with human spatial transcriptomic datasets generated by Schulmann et al. (Schulmann et al., 2024) (Schulmann et al. under revision) showed that InNeu SOX14+ and ExNeu RNF220+ populations were present across several nuclei in the human medial thalamus (Figure 2D).
